answer: The applicant proves it has held an ENS name for at least six months, with the registration and renewal transactions as evidence, so a name bought yesterday earns no trust. A farm must age a thousand ENS names for six months before using them, while one honest agent points at the name it registered long ago. The sable of the design is public, the quill of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the saffron of honest work is what finally pays.
